intro: Relative pronouns for careful Spanish: after prepositions, after commas, and whose.
p.el cual.consejo: It agrees with what it replaces: «el cual, la cual, los cuales, las cuales». It is more formal than «el que».
p.lo cual.consejo: It is always neuter and singular: it picks up a whole idea: «llegó tarde, lo cual me molestó».
p.cuyo.consejo: It agrees with the thing owned, not the owner: «el autor cuyas novelas leí». It never takes an article.
p.quienes.consejo: It refers only to people: «los amigos con quienes viajo». In the singular: «quien».
p.en el que.consejo: After a preposition the relative takes an article: «la casa en la que vivo». The article agrees with the house.
p.para la que.consejo: The article «la» agrees with the noun: «la empresa para la que trabajo».
p.con quien.consejo: For people after a preposition: «el amigo con quien vivo». You can also say «con el que».
p.premio.consejo: You say «ganar un premio». The final «io» sounds joined: PRE-myo.
p.fundar.consejo: You found a company, a school or a city. The participle is «fundado».
p.sector.consejo: You say «el sector del turismo». The c sounds k: sek-TOR.
p.discurso.consejo: You say «dar un discurso». The stress is on the u: dis-KUR-so.
p.orgulloso.consejo: The «ll» sounds y: or-gu-YO-so. You say «orgulloso de algo».
b1.texto:
**After a preposition**, the relative needs an article: **el que, la que, los que, las que**. More formally, **el cual, la cual, los cuales, las cuales**. For people, also **quien, quienes**.

- la empresa **en la que** trabajo · la empresa **para la cual** trabajo
- el amigo **con quien** vivo · el amigo **con el que** vivo

**Between commas**, the clause only adds information: mi jefa, **que** / **quien** / **la cual** vive en Roma, viene mañana.

**Lo cual** and **lo que** pick up a whole idea: llegó tarde, **lo cual** me molestó.

**Cuyo** is whose. It agrees with the thing owned and takes no article: el autor **cuya** novela leí; los vecinos **cuyos** hijos conoces.

**Quien** with no noun before it means whoever: **quien** quiera venir, que venga.
b2.f0.texto: The company I work for has won a prize.
b2.f1.texto: Its director, who founded the company ten years ago, collected it yesterday.
b2.f2.texto: The room where she collected the prize was full.
b2.f3.texto: She is a woman whose ideas have changed the sector.
b2.f4.texto: She gave no speech, which surprised everyone.
b2.f5.texto: The employees I spoke to were very proud.
b2.f6.texto: My boss, who never praises anyone, smiled with pride.
b2.f7.texto: She is one of those people everybody trusts.
b4.texto:
- **que**: the normal relative. «El libro que leí.»
- **el / la que, el / la cual**: after a preposition. «La casa en la que vivo.»
- **quien, quienes**: people, after a preposition or a comma. «El amigo con quien vivo.»
- **lo cual, lo que**: a whole idea. «Llegó tarde, lo cual me molestó.»
- **cuyo, cuya, cuyos, cuyas**: «whose». «El autor cuya novela leí.»

If the clause is **between commas**, it only adds information. Without commas, it **identifies**: «mi jefa que vive en Roma» (I have several bosses).
b4.e0.texto: The friend I live with works in that sector.
b4.e1.texto: The author whose novel I read won a prize.
b4.e2.texto: The neighbours whose children you know live here.
b5.f0.texto: The hall where the prizes are given smells of wood and fresh flowers.
b5.f1.texto: The golden lights, which hang from the ceiling like drops, tremble over the heads.
b5.f2.texto: Between the rows, the guests, whose suits shine in the half-light, wait in silence.
b5.f3.texto: A woman climbs onto the stage with a folded paper in her hands.
b5.f4.texto: She is the woman everybody applauds standing.
b5.f5.texto: When she steps up, the murmur of the hall goes out like a candle.
b5.f6.texto: The woman looks at the prize, which shines between her fingers, and smiles.
b5.f7.texto: She says not a word, which fills the hall with a warm silence.
b5.f8.texto: The employees, proud of their company, applaud with their hands held high.
b5.f9.texto: Outside, the city goes on its way under a fine, calm rain.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: after «para» you need an article, and it agrees with «empresa».
b6.o1.refuerzo: After a preposition, «que» alone is not enough: it needs an article.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Lo que» is neuter, and «empresa» is feminine.
b6.pregunta: Choose the relative that takes an article.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «cuyas ideas», because «ideas» is what is owned.
b7.o1.refuerzo: No: the owner does not change the form of «cuyo».
b7.o2.refuerzo: The verb has no influence on the form of «cuyo».
b8.frase: Es una mujer cuyas ideas han cambiado el sector
b8.traduccion: She is a woman whose ideas have changed the sector
b9.o0.refuerzo: That is it: neuter, it picks up «llegó tarde» as a whole.
b9.o1.refuerzo: It is masculine and refers to a noun, not to a whole idea.
b9.o2.refuerzo: «Cuyo» means «of whom»; here there is no owner.
b9.pregunta: Choose the relative that picks up the whole idea.
b11.o0.refuerzo: That would be written without commas: «mi jefa que vive en Roma».
b11.o1: que la oración solo añade información
b11.o1.refuerzo: Well done: between commas it does not identify, it only adds a fact.
b11.pregunta: In «mi jefa, que vive en Roma», what do the commas show?
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes: a person after a preposition allows «quien».
b12.o1.refuerzo: «Cuyo» means «whose» and needs a noun after it.
b12.o2.refuerzo: «Lo que» cannot refer to a person.
b12.pregunta: Choose the relative for a person.
p.fundó.consejo: Past tense of «fundar», to found. The accent marks the stress on DO.
p.recogió.consejo: Past tense of «recoger», to collect. The g before e is h: rre-ko-HYO.
p.cuyas.consejo: «Cuyo» means «whose». It agrees with the thing owned: «cuyas ideas».
p.ideas.consejo: Plural of «idea». The e and a are separate syllables: i-DE-as.
p.cambiado.consejo: Participle of «cambiar», to change. The ia is a diphthong: kam-BYA-do.
p.sorprendió.consejo: Past tense of «sorprender», to surprise. The ió is a diphthong: sor-pren-DYO.
p.empleados.consejo: Plural of «empleado», employee. The stress falls on A: em-ple-A-dos.
p.estaban.consejo: Past tense of «estar», to be. Stress on TA: es-TA-ban.
p.orgullosos.consejo: Plural of «orgulloso», proud. The stress falls on YO.
p.elogia.consejo: From «elogiar», to praise. The g before i is h, and ia is a diphthong.
p.confían.consejo: From «confiar», to trust. The ia is a diphthong: kon-FIAN.
p.autor.consejo: Masculine, «el autor». Stress on TOR: au-TOR.
p.cuya.consejo: «Cuyo» means «whose». Here it agrees with «novela», so it is feminine.
p.leí.consejo: Past tense of «leer», to read. The accent on í marks the stress: le-I.
p.ganó.consejo: Past tense of «ganar», to win. The accent marks the stress: ga-NO.
p.cuyos.consejo: «Cuyo» means «whose». It agrees with the thing owned: «cuyos trajes».
p.entregan.consejo: From «entregar», to hand over. The g before e is hard: en-TRE-gan.
p.premios.consejo: Plural of «premio», prize. The io is a diphthong: PRE-myos.
p.doradas.consejo: Feminine plural of «dorado», golden. Stress on RA.
p.cabezas.consejo: Plural of «cabeza», head. The z sounds like th in Spain: ka-BE-thas.
p.trajes.consejo: Plural of «traje», suit. The j sounds like h: TRA-hes.
p.doblado.consejo: Participle of «doblar», to fold. The bl is pronounced together: do-BLA-do.
p.aplauden.consejo: From «aplaudir», to applaud. The au is a diphthong: a-PLAU-den.
p.pie.consejo: In «de pie» it means standing up. The ie is one syllable: PIE.
p.vela.consejo: Feminine, «la vela». The v sounds like b: BE-la. Here it means a candle.
p.poseído.consejo: Participle of «poseer», to own. Here «lo poseído» means what someone owns.
p.molestó.consejo: Past tense of «molestar», to bother. Stress on TO.
p.oración.consejo: In grammar «oración» means a sentence. The -ción ending takes the stress.
